title: AI Medical Interpretation in Genetic Counseling
summary: AI medical interpretation in genetic counseling can protect pedigrees, probability, uncertain results, consent, and patient understanding.
body_markdown:
###


Yes. In a U.S. genetics program, AI interpretation with defined quality controls can support pedigree intake, pretest education, consent discussions, results disclosure, and follow-up when the intended language and workflow have been tested. Human interpreters remain complementary according to patient preference, organizational policy, and encounter needs.


###


The counselor should state one probability at a time, give both a fraction and percentage when useful, and ask the patient to explain the meaning in their own words. In a clinical genetics visit, the counselor retains responsibility for the risk calculation, while the interpreter preserves the stated number, qualifier, and time frame.


###


The care team should pause and clarify the biological relationship instead of selecting the closest English label. In a pedigree workflow, ask which side of the family the person belongs to, whether the relationship is biological, and how the family describes the relationship in plain language before documenting it.


###


No. Opalite Health supports healthcare-specific spoken interpretation across 150+ languages and dialects, but the genetic counselor or other qualified clinician explains the test result and makes clinical decisions. Spoken interpretation carries that explanation between languages; it does not classify variants, calculate recurrence risk, or recommend care.


###


No. In U.S. clinical genetics, a variant of uncertain significance means available evidence does not establish whether the variant contributes to disease. The clinician should explain the laboratory’s classification and follow the applicable genetics guidance rather than presenting the result as positive, negative, or diagnostic.
